title: Navier-Stokes hydrodynamics near the critical point with out-of-equilibrium modes
authors: Md Hasanujjaman, Golam Sarwar, Mahfuzur Rahaman, Abhijit Bhattacharyya, Jane Alam
abstract: We investigate how slow out-of-equilibrium modes (OEM), introduced to extend the regime of validity of hydrodynamics near the critical point, fundamentally reshape the power spectrum of dynamical density fluctuations. We have used the equation of motion of slow modes for the situation when the extensive nature of thermodynamics is not altered due to the introduction of OEM. We find that the extensivity condition puts an extra constraint on the coupling of OEM with the four divergence of velocity. In the absence of OEM, the dynamic structure factor exhibits three Lorentzian peaks, one at zero frequency ($ω$), called Rayleigh peak and the other two called Brillouin peaks located symmetrically about $ω=0$. When the system is away from the critical point the inclusion of the OEM preserves the symmetry of the distributions but all the peaks acquire reduced widths and the Brillouin peaks adopt unequal heights. Irrespective of the value of OEM (zero or nonzero) the Brillouin peaks vanish near the critical point. The width of the Rayleigh peak substantially reduced in presence of OEM. Such reductions of the widths in presence of the OEM indicates the reduction in the decay rate of the fluctuation which leads to slowing down of decay of the fluctuations, a distinctive feature of the critical point.
summary: This paper develops an extended hydrodynamic theory by incorporating slow out-of-equilibrium modes (OEM) to describe fluid dynamics near a critical point. By analyzing the dynamic structure factor, the authors show that the OEM fundamentally alters the spectral signature, causing the disappearance of Brillouin peaks and a marked narrowing of the Rayleigh peak. This narrowing signifies a critical slowing down of fluctuations.
main_problem: The study investigates how incorporating slow out-of-equilibrium modes (OEM) modifies the power spectrum of density fluctuations in fluid dynamics near a critical point, extending the validity of standard hydrodynamics.
main_result: The inclusion of OEM causes the Brillouin peaks to vanish near the critical point and substantially reduces the width of the Rayleigh peak, signaling a slowing down of fluctuation decay rate.
method: The authors use linear mode analysis on the augmented hydrodynamic equations (Hydro+ scheme), derived by ensuring thermodynamic consistency with the second law of thermodynamics.
model_or_system: The system is a fluid undergoing dynamics near a critical point, modeled using Navier-Stokes equations augmented by a relaxation equation for the slow mode $\phi$.
key_observables: The dynamic structure factor, $S_{hoho}(k,\omega)$, which exhibits Rayleigh and Brillouin peaks.
important_parameters: Temperature relative to the critical temperature ($T/T_c$), wave number ($k$), and the coupling parameters associated with the OEM ($ ar{\phi}, b$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the change in transport coefficients due to the OEM is small, and it linearizes the full hydrodynamic equations around equilibrium.
figures_summary: Figures compare $S_{hoho}(k,\omega)$ away from and near the critical point, showing the effect of $\phi$ on peak structure, and illustrate the dependence of peak heights on the OEM parameters $ ar{\phi}$ and $b$.
paper_structure: The paper builds the formalism by deriving the OEM evolution equation from the entropy production principle, linearizes the resulting coupled hydrodynamic equations, and finally calculates the dynamic structure factor $S_{hoho}(k,\omega)$ to analyze the spectral changes.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of thermodynamic consistency principles to extend hydrodynamic descriptions into non-equilibrium regimes, especially near critical points, provides advanced tools for understanding critical dynamics relevant to many-body systems.
